Compare transition probabilities between groups with a Bayesian model

Source: R/bayes_compare_lsa.R
bayes_compare_lsa.Rd

bayes_compare_lsa() compares the transition probabilities of groups with a Bayesian model: given the counts, it estimates the plausible range of the true difference between two groups' transition probabilities and how precisely that difference is estimated. Under a Dirichlet-Multinomial model the outgoing transitions of each state are a multinomial draw whose probabilities have a Dirichlet posterior, so each transition probability has a Beta posterior in each group. A transition whose source state is rarely visited gets a wide interval, even when its estimated probabilities look far apart. A permutation test (compare_lsa()) instead tests whether a group difference is larger than chance.

For every transition, bayes_compare_lsa() computes the posterior mean difference of the transition probability between two groups (exact), its credible interval and the probability of direction (the posterior probability of the more probable sign of the difference), both from Monte Carlo draws of the Beta posteriors, and a standardised effect size. A transition is credibly different when its credible interval excludes zero, the absolute mean difference exceeds mean_threshold, and the interval end nearest zero lies further from zero than bound_threshold; the thresholds keep detectable but negligible differences out. With more than two groups every pair is compared. No resampling of sequences is involved, so the comparison is fast.

The model treats transitions as independent draws and compares transition probabilities only. For a test that respects the dependence between events of one sequence, or that compares adjusted residuals or odds ratios, use compare_lsa(). For the posterior of one group's transition probabilities, use certainty_lsa().

Usage

bayes_compare_lsa(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  prior = 0.5,
  draws = 10000L,
  ci = 0.95,
  mean_threshold = 0.01,
  bound_threshold = 0.001,
  adjust = "none",
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_bayes'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_bayes_pairwise'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A grouped fit from lsa(data, group = ) with two or more groups, or the lsa fit of the first group. For the print() methods, the comparison result.

y

The lsa fit of the second group when x is a single fit (the groups are then labelled "a" and "b"). Default NULL.

prior

Dirichlet concentration added to every cell. Default 0.5 (the Jeffreys prior); 1 gives a uniform prior.

draws

Number of Monte Carlo draws for the credible intervals. Default 10000.

ci

Credible-interval level. Default 0.95.

mean_threshold

Minimum absolute posterior mean difference for a transition to be credibly different. Default 0.01.

bound_threshold

Minimum distance from zero of the interval end nearest zero. Default 0.001.

adjust

Multiple-comparison correction applied to the two-sided Bayesian p-value 2 * (1 - pd) across transitions (and across all pairs for more than two groups); any method of stats::p.adjust(). Default "none". It changes the p_adj column only: the significant flag is decided by the credible interval and the thresholds.

seed

Optional seed for the Monte Carlo draws. Default NULL. The session's random number state is restored on exit.

...

Not used.

Value

With two groups, an object of class c("lsa_bayes", "lsa_comparison", "list"); with more than two, an object of class c("lsa_bayes_pairwise", "lsa_comparison_pairwise", "list"). Read the per-transition table with transitions(): one row per transition (from -> to pair), and for more than two groups one row per transition and pair of groups, with the columns

  • group_a, group_b (more than two groups only): the pair compared;

  • from, to: source and target state;

  • prob_a, prob_b: posterior mean transition probability in each group;

  • diff: prob_a - prob_b; ci_low, ci_high: its credible interval;

  • pd: probability of direction; effect_size: diff divided by its posterior standard deviation;

  • p_value: 2 * (1 - pd) (NA for transitions that cannot be estimated); p_adj: after adjust;

  • significant: credibly different.

transitions(x, significant = TRUE) keeps the credibly different transitions; sort = "strength" orders by the absolute difference. as.data.frame(x, what = "global") gives the number of credibly different transitions per pair of groups (see as.data.frame.lsa_comparison()); plot() draws the differences. print() shows the settings and the number of credibly different transitions and returns x invisibly.

Conditions

Errors carry the class lagdynamics_error and one of:

  • lagdynamics_needs_events: a fit was built from a transition matrix.

  • lagdynamics_incompatible_fits: the groups differ in their states, engine, lag or structural zeros.

  • lagdynamics_bad_input: adjust is not a method of stats::p.adjust(); x is neither a grouped fit nor an lsa fit with a second fit in y; y is given together with a grouped fit; or the grouped fit has fewer than two groups.

References

Johnston, L., & Jendoubi, T. (2026). How delivery mode reshapes resource engagement: A Bayesian differential network analysis. TNA Workshop 2026.

See also

transitions() and as.data.frame.lsa_comparison() to read the result; plot.lsa_comparison() to draw it; compare_lsa() for the permutation test; certainty_lsa() for one group's posterior.

Examples

g <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
         time = "Time", group = "Achiever")
bc <- bayes_compare_lsa(g, adjust = "BH", seed = 1)
bc
#> <lsa_bayes>  (Bayesian Dirichlet-Multinomial comparison)
#>   groups:    High vs Low
#>   prior:     Dirichlet(0.50)  |  draws: 10000  |  CI: 95%
#>   edges:     38 credibly different of 81 compared
transitions(bc, significant = TRUE, sort = "strength") |> head()
#>        from        to    prob_a     prob_b        diff      ci_low     ci_high
#> 1   discuss consensus 0.4241594 0.21434059  0.20981881  0.18162651  0.23797612
#> 2 synthesis consensus 0.5681416 0.38177015  0.18637145  0.10922167  0.26011889
#> 3 synthesis     adapt 0.1433628 0.29986790 -0.15650507 -0.21785545 -0.09399030
#> 4 synthesis      plan 0.1433628 0.02509908  0.11826376  0.07644129  0.16412292
#> 5 consensus   discuss 0.2324452 0.13649499  0.09595018  0.07709173  0.11529950
#> 6   discuss     adapt 0.0241594 0.12010243 -0.09594303 -0.11191197 -0.08030344
#>   pd effect_size p_value p_adj significant
#> 1  1   14.555641       0     0        TRUE
#> 2  1    4.863305       0     0        TRUE
#> 3  1   -4.965182       0     0        TRUE
#> 4  1    5.301216       0     0        TRUE
#> 5  1    9.918048       0     0        TRUE
#> 6  1  -11.770044       0     0        TRUE

# Three courses: every pair
courses <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
               time = "Time", group = "Course")
bayes_compare_lsa(courses, draws = 2000, seed = 1) |>
  as.data.frame(what = "global")
#>   group_a group_b n_credible
#> 1       A       B         31
#> 2       A       C         31
#> 3       B       C          4
